input.body:
label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The Export button remains disabled after a failed export because the `busy` state is not reset when `exportReport` rejects. The fix should catch the rejection and set `busy` to `false` to re-enable the button.

input.title: Re-enable the Export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` function in the `ExportButton` component sets `busy` to `true` at the start of the export process but only resets it to `false` in the `.then()` callback, which executes **only if the export succeeds**. If the export fails (e.g., due to a server error), the `busy` state remains `true`, disabling the button permanently. To fix this, the `exportReport` call should include a `.catch()` handler that also sets `busy` to `false`, ensuring the button is re-enabled after any export attempt, successful or not.

input.title: Re-enable the Export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` function in the `ExportButton` component sets `busy` to `true` at the start of the export process but only resets it to `false` in the `.then()` callback, which executes **only if the export succeeds**. If the export fails (e.g., due to a server error), the `busy` state remains `true`, disabling the button permanently. To fix this, the `exportReport` call should include a `.catch()` handler that also sets `busy` to `false`, ensuring the button is re-enabled after any export attempt, successful or not.
